items.textToSpeech: For everyone aged 14+, including those pregnant or lactating, the Upper Level of Intake for iron is 45 milligrams per day. Those who are homozygous for hereditary haemochromatosis are particularly susceptible to iron overload, even at normal dietary iron intakes. Such individuals should avoid iron supplements and highly iron-fortified foods. The majority of homozygotes are not diagnosed or identified until sufficient iron has accumulated to produce adverse effects.

The Upper Level of Intake is the highest average daily nutrient intake level likely to pose no adverse health effects to almost all individuals in the general population. For Australia and New Zealand, Nutrient Reference Values are published by the National Health and Medical Research Council. Is there anything else I can help you with?
